Subject: Question on prepay sweep / burn curve for multi-year commit

Ben — thanks again for the demo last week. Finance asked me to confirm a couple of details before we put the numbers into our model.

1) If we do a 3-year agreement with an annual prepay (Year 1: $1.2M, Year 2: $900k, Year 3: $600k), how do credits burn down if our usage ramps unevenly (big Q1/Q2 spike, quieter Q3)? Do credits sit in a single wallet and sweep monthly, or can you amortize at the year level with a smoothing curve?

2) Does Redwood allow a drawdown that prioritizes committed tokens for low-latency routes (we have a mix of standard and premium endpoints)?

3) Any restrictions on carryforward between years? Our procurement prefers a small carryover (up to 10%) but wants to avoid large shelf credits.

I've attached a 6-month usage sample to illustrate the ramp we're expecting. Can you and finance sketch a sample burn curve and proposed invoice timing so we can include it in our internal approval?

Thanks — Elena

Subject: Re: Question on prepay sweep / burn curve for multi-year commit

Elena — appreciate the clear usage sample. High level answers first, then a sketch of a few options attached: RDW_prepay_credit_curve_v1.xlsx.

- Wallet model: by default the prepay is deposited into a tenant-level wallet that draws down on a first-in, weighted-usage basis. That means monthly sweep/consumption by actual tokens.

- Amortized curve: we offer an amortization profile as an optional billing construct for multi-year commits. That lets you smooth the effective monthly expense (useful for internal GAAP/procurement), with the underlying credits still sitting in the wallet for operational routing.

- Route prioritization: yes — you can configure route-level prioritization so committed credits preferentially cover premium routes. We expose that as a routing policy in the contract and console.

- Carryforward: standard is 0% carryforward between years on annual prepay; we can grant up to 10% carryforward on Year 1->Year 2 for multi-year deals, but carryforward beyond that is subject to a step-down discount. We put these terms into the SOW when agreed.

I've attached two sample curves in the spreadsheet: (A) "sweep-first" (credits drawn on actual usage monthly) and (B) "amortized smooth" (monthly effective burn rate smoothed across the year with a quarterly reconciliation). See tab 'Illustrative Curves'.

Can you confirm whether Omega needs the smooth accounting profile (procurement sign-off) or prefers operational sweep (simpler)? If procurement needs the smooth profile we'll loop legal/finance for SOW language.

I'll get Rishi to propose the exact invoicing cadence given the numbers.

—Ben

- If actual spend < amortized amount and carryforward is enabled (10%), how is the leftover tracked and shown on your billing statements?

For context, Omega wants predictable P&L treatment for FY27 and to avoid unexpected cash calls during peak periods.

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on prepay sweep / burn curve for multi-year commit

Carlos — great questions. Short answers here and I can draft the billing paragraph for the SOW once you confirm the approach.

- Overages: operationally, the wallet will cover any overage in the month it occurs (no automatic cash call). If the wallet balance depletes and you exceed committed tokens, we will trigger an overage invoice T+30 for incremental consumption. For amortized smoothing we will reconcile quarterly: if cumulative actual > cumulative amortized at reconciliation, the overage is invoiced; if cumulative actual < cumulative amortized and carryforward applies, leftover credits are carried forward up to the agreed cap.

- Year-end reconciliation: we produce a reconciliation report showing monthly amortized vs actual consumption and the remaining wallet balance. For accounting teams, we can provide a journal-friendly export (CSV) and a one-line invoice adjustment if needed to zero out differences when the contract specifies that treatment.

- Visibility: all of this is surfaced in Redwood Console under Billing -> Commitment Ledger. You can set alerts for when cumulative actual exceeds X% of cumulative amortized.

If Omega wants to avoid deferred revenue entries entirely, option A is operational sweep (no amortization) — simpler: prepay consumed as used, no quarterly recon except for reporting. Option B is amortized with quarterly reconciliation and overage invoicing. Option C is amortized + automatic top-up (pre-approved cc/PO) — we avoid auto-captures by default but can include top-up with explicit terms.

Which option is procurement leaning to? I can draft SOW text with the chosen option and carryforward limits.

Thanks — Rishi
